title: Constant Weil twist
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-wf-weil-category]:
$k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $q=p^a$, $a\geq1$, $k=\overline{k_0}$,
$\ell\ne p$, and $\Qlb=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$.
Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, put
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $P_E=\Phi_X^*$ be the geometric-Frobenius
pullback in the finite-stage PBC coefficient category of that definition.
For $b\in\Qlb^\times$, let $E$ be a finite intermediate extension
$E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ containing $b$, for instance $E=\mathbf Q_\ell(b)$
[def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set].
No integrality or valuation-zero condition is imposed on $b$.

Here is the coefficient object and Frobenius map used in this definition.
Write $\mathcal O_E$ for the valuation ring of $E$ and choose a
uniformizer $\varpi_E$. Put $R_E=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}
(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_X$ on the small pro-etale site.
Take the constant degree-zero object $U_E^{\mathrm{sf}}$ obtained by
rationalizing $R_E[0]$ [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible]
and its canonical isomorphism
$\theta_E:\Phi_X^{*,\mathrm{sf}}U_E^{\mathrm{sf}}\xrightarrow{\sim}
U_E^{\mathrm{sf}}$ of [def-weil-constant-weil-structure].
Use precisely the coefficient equivalence and Frobenius comparison of
[lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison]. Write
$U_E=J_{X,E}(U_E^{\mathrm{sf}})$ and write that comparison in the direction
$$c_E:P_EJ_{X,E}(U_E^{\mathrm{sf}})\xrightarrow{\sim}
J_{X,E}(\Phi_X^{*,\mathrm{sf}}U_E^{\mathrm{sf}}).$$
Set $e_E=J_{X,E}(\theta_E)\circ c_E:P_EU_E\xrightarrow{\sim}U_E$.
Thus $U_E$ has the actual integral representative $R_E[0]$ in the raw
rationalization prescribed by [def-wf-weil-category]; it is not an
unidentified sheaf in a different coefficient model.

The *constant Weil line* with scalar $b$ is the common-stage object
$$\mathcal B_b:=\bigl(E,(U_E,b e_E)\bigr)
\quad\text{in }\mathrm{WeilD}(X_0,\Qlb).$$
Here $b e_E$ is multiplication by $b$ after $e_E$, in the rationalized
Hom group, with inverse $e_E^{-1}\circ(b^{-1}\operatorname{id}_{U_E})$.
For $E\subset L$ containing $b$, the objects built at $E$ and at $L$ are
compared by the canonical constant-object isomorphism $\alpha_{E,L}$ of
[lem-weil-constant-weil-structure-stage-independence], transported to PBC as
$$J_{X,L}(\alpha_{E,L})\circ j_{X,L/E,U_E^{\mathrm{sf}}}^{-1}:
T^{\mathrm{pbc}}_{L/E}U_E\xrightarrow{\sim}U_L;$$
unrelated finite stages are compared through their finite compositum.
The construction applies to every separated finite-type $X_0$, including
disconnected and empty ones.

For a constructible Weil complex $\mathcal F$ on $X_0$ (in particular a
constructible Weil sheaf), its *constant Weil twist* by $b$ is
$\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal B_b$, the completed derived tensor with the
tensor Frobenius of [def-wf-tensor-product] at a common finite
coefficient stage, read in the common-stage convention of
[def-wf-weil-category].

Relation to the source characterization (a remark, not part of the
data). When $X_0$ is geometrically connected, $W(X_0)$ and
$\deg:W(X_0)\to\mathbf Z$ are those of [def-wf-weil-group], and the
Weil fundamental representation is that of
[def-wf-fundamental-representation]. The source defines $\mathcal B_b$ as
the rank-one Weil sheaf with representation $g\mapsto b^{\deg(g)}$,
trivial on $\pi_1(X)$. That the line constructed above is lisse of rank
one, is independent of $E$ up to the identifications above (which are
Weil-pair isomorphisms), has exactly this representation, and that for a
constructible Weil sheaf $(M,\theta)$ the twist is identified, through the
completed right-unit map, with $(M,b\theta)$, are theorems about this
construction. They are proved in the lemma
`lem-wf-constant-twist-coefficient-comparison`, which cites this
definition; they are not assumed here.
